Cells within 50 km of this point are called known for a site that is elsewhere, and cells at the real sites are not.

top_places.name: New Siberian Islands, Russia (Bunge Land and Kotelny)
top_places.hosts_analog_or_polar_field_work: Yes, polar science but no space-analog use found. Bunge Land is a 6,200 km2 bare sand plain between Kotelny and Faddeyevsky, studied by Russian and German permafrost teams (Schirrmeister and others 2010) and shown by NASA Earth Observatory. Kotelny had a research station and base from 1933 to 1993; the Temp airfield is now military.

evidence.claim: Bunge Land: about 6,200 km2 of sand, mostly under 8 m above the sea, origin studied by Schirrmeister et al. 2010
NASA Earth Observatory image story on the sandy plains
Kotelny: research station and base 1933 to 1993, Temp airfield to be rebuilt by the Northern Fleet

top_places.not_checked: Whether the airfield or base operates now; permits (the area is a military zone). The article date was not shown.

top_places.name: Nordaustlandet, Svalbard (Murchisonfjorden)
top_places.hosts_analog_or_polar_field_work: Yes, both. The ESA / Open University catalogue lists Murchison Fjord (79.88 N 18.49 E) as an AMASE Mars-analog site. The Kinnvika station in the same fjord was built for the International Geophysical Year 1957-58 and used again in 2007-09; it is empty now. The place is polar desert inside the Nordaust-Svalbard nature reserve. It is not a little-known place.

evidence.claim: Catalogue chapter 26.6.3: Murchison Fjord, prior analogue usage AMASE
Kinnvika: built 1957-58 by a Swedish-Finnish-Swiss expedition, revived for the Polar Year 2007-09, inside the nature reserve

top_places.not_checked: Which AMASE years worked there; current landing and research permit rules of the reserve.
